summary: Specifies the Neighbor Discovery protocol for IPv6, which lets hosts and routers find each other on a link and learn about nearby network details. It is on the standards track as a proposed standard. It was replaced by RFC 2461.

eli5.summary: When you move into a new neighborhood, you look around to see who lives next door and where the exits are. This is how computers do it.

questions: how do ipv6 hosts find neighbors
how to discover routers in ipv6
subtitle: How IPv6 nodes find each other and learn network details on a local link

tldr.problem: IPv6 nodes on the same link need to find each other, learn about nearby routers, and maintain reachability information without the scattered mechanisms used in IPv4.
tldr.mechanism: Neighbor Discovery defines five ICMP message types: Router Solicitation and Advertisement for finding routers and learning prefixes, Neighbor Solicitation and Advertisement for address resolution, and Redirect messages for better routing paths.
tldr.outcome: IPv6 networks automatically discover neighbors and configure themselves without manual intervention. RFC 2461 replaced this specification with updates to the protocol.

today: RFC 1970 was superseded by RFC 2461, which updated the Neighbor Discovery specification for IPv6. RFC 2461 is the current standard for IPv6 Neighbor Discovery.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Neighbor Discovery is a protocol for IPv6 nodes to discover each other's presence and link-layer addresses on the same link, find routers willing to forward packets, and maintain reachability information. The protocol handles router discovery, prefix discovery, address autoconfiguration, address resolution, detection of neighbor failure, duplicate address detection, and redirection to better paths.

IPv6 Neighbor Discovery combines and improves upon three separate IPv4 protocols: ARP (for address resolution), ICMP Router Discovery (for finding routers), and ICMP Redirect. Unlike IPv4, Neighbor Discovery is a core part of IPv6, providing mechanisms for hosts to automatically configure themselves without manual intervention.
sections.eli5: This is how IPv6 computers automatically discover routers nearby, learn what addresses they can use, and find out how to reach other computers on the same network.

sections.title: Message Types
sections.content:
Neighbor Discovery defines five ICMP message types. Router Solicitation (type 133) asks routers to advertise themselves immediately. Router Advertisement (type 134) announces a router's presence with prefixes for address configuration and link parameters like hop limit and MTU. Neighbor Solicitation (type 135) asks a neighbor for its link-layer address or to verify reachability. Neighbor Advertisement (type 136) responds with the sender's link-layer address. Redirect (type 137) informs a host of a better first-hop neighbor for a destination.

Each message includes an ICMP checksum and validation of the hop limit (always 255 for Neighbor Discovery messages). Messages can include optional fields like source and target link-layer addresses, prefix information, redirected headers, and MTU values.
sections.eli5: The protocol uses five types of ICMP messages: routers say hello and tell computers what addresses to use, computers ask for a neighbor's address, computers respond with their address, and routers say to use a different path.

sections.title: Router and Prefix Discovery
sections.content:
When a host's interface becomes active, it can send Router Solicitation messages to prompt routers to advertise immediately, rather than waiting for the next scheduled advertisement. Routers periodically multicast Router Advertisements announcing their presence, along with prefixes that define which addresses are on-link. Hosts use these advertisements to build a list of default routers and learn which addresses are reachable directly on the link without going through a router.

Router Advertisement messages carry link-layer addresses, network parameters, and information for address autoconfiguration. This centralizes configuration on routers and eliminates the need for separate address configuration mechanisms. Hosts can also learn that a destination is on-link through Redirect messages when a router identifies a better path.
sections.eli5: Routers announce themselves and tell computers what addresses are local. Computers listen to these announcements to learn how to find neighbors and configure their own addresses.

sections.title: Address Resolution and Reachability
sections.content:
When a node needs to send a packet to an on-link destination but does not know the link-layer address, it sends a Neighbor Solicitation multicast to the solicited-node multicast address derived from the target's IP address. The target responds with a unicast Neighbor Advertisement containing its link-layer address. This request-response pair lets both the initiator and target learn each other's link-layer addresses.

Neighbor Unreachability Detection uses Neighbor Solicitation messages to verify that neighbors are still reachable. When a node is actively sending traffic to a neighbor, it occasionally sends probe messages to ensure the neighbor still responds. If a neighbor fails to respond after multiple probes, the node marks it unreachable and selects an alternate router if needed. Neighbor Advertisements sent in response to solicitations serve as explicit reachability confirmation.
sections.eli5: When a computer wants to send a packet to a neighbor, it asks 'who has this address?' and the neighbor responds with its link-layer address. To check if a neighbor is still working, the computer asks periodically and expects an answer.

sections.title: Advanced Features
sections.content:
Neighbor Discovery handles several important scenarios. Link-layer address changes are announced through unsolicited Neighbor Advertisement multicast messages, quickly updating cached addresses. Nodes can load-balance incoming traffic across multiple interfaces with the same link-layer address by including or omitting source link-layer addresses. Anycast addresses (shared by multiple nodes) are handled by allowing multiple Neighbor Advertisements for the same target. Routers can proxy Neighbor Advertisements on behalf of nodes that cannot respond, useful for mobile nodes that move off-link.

The protocol supports diverse link types: multicast-capable links (Ethernet), point-to-point links (PPP), non-broadcast multi-access links (ATM, Frame Relay), shared media links, and links with variable MTUs. Neighbor Discovery is extensible through new option types, allowing future additions without breaking implementations that ignore unknown options.
sections.eli5: The protocol handles special cases like when a computer moves and gets a new link-layer address, when multiple computers share the same address, and when routers need to handle computers that cannot respond directly.

sections.title: Security
sections.content:
Neighbor Discovery messages use a hop limit of 255, which prevents off-link attackers from sending ND messages that would be accepted by on-link nodes. However, on-link attackers can still forge Neighbor Discovery messages. Authentication can be provided using IP authentication headers between trusted neighbors. The protocol specifies that implementations should validate message contents and ignore malformed or unexpected messages.

Neighbor Unreachability Detection provides robustness by detecting when a neighbor or path has failed, allowing nodes to switch to alternate routes before relying on broken connections. Using link-local addresses to identify routers ensures that host-router associations survive even when the site renumbers to new global prefixes.
sections.eli5: The protocol uses tricks like requiring a hop limit of 255 to prevent off-link attackers from fooling on-link computers. Authentication headers can protect against on-link attacks.
